title: Contact patch test: two blocks with non-matching meshes in uniaxial compression (implicit mortar contact)
source: The contact patch test: a contact discretisation must transmit a uniform pressure across a non-matching interface exactly; Taylor & Papadopoulos, On a patch test for contact problems in two dimensions, Nonlinear Computational Mechanics, Springer 1991, 690–702; Crisfield, Re-visiting the contact patch test, IJNME 48:435–449, 2000; passed by mortar methods: Puso & Laursen, CMAME 193:601–629, 2004. Uniaxial stress between frictionless symmetry planes is uniform in both blocks

quantities.quantity: Small: σ_zz of the lower block's corner element under the interface (element 10) over that of the upper block's corner element over it (element 19)
quantities.reason: small sliding is linear and its mortar integrals exact on these rectangular faces: a uniform stress is the discrete solution up to the convergence tolerance (10⁻¹⁰)

quantities.quantity: Small: σ_zz of the lower block's centre element under the interface (element 14) over that of element 19
Small: σ_zz of the lower block's bottom corner element (element 1) over that of element 19
Small: σ_zz of the upper block's top far corner element (element 26) over that of element 19
Small: σ_xx of element 14 over its σ_zz (uniaxial stress: 0)
quantities.reason: frictionless symmetry planes and a frictionless interface leave the blocks free to expand sideways; the non-matching interface must not hold them

quantities.quantity: Small: the contact pressure at the secondary node (0.5, 0.5, 1) over −σ_zz of element 19
quantities.reason: the mortar multipliers are the nodal values of the contact pressure, uniform and equal to the stress across the interface

quantities.quantity: Small: the integrated contact pressure over the reaction at the pushed top
quantities.reason: the pressure carries the whole load across the interface

quantities.quantity: Finite: σ_zz of the lower block's corner element under the interface (element 10) over that of the upper block's corner element over it (element 19)
quantities.reason: finite sliding is exact up to the geometric terms of the gaps the augmentation leaves (10⁻⁵ of the element thickness) and the default convergence tolerances

quantities.quantity: Finite: σ_zz of the lower block's centre element under the interface (element 14) over that of element 19
Finite: σ_zz of the lower block's bottom corner element (element 1) over that of element 19
Finite: σ_zz of the upper block's top far corner element (element 26) over that of element 19
Finite: σ_xx of element 14 over its σ_zz (uniaxial stress: 0)
quantities.reason: frictionless symmetry planes and a frictionless interface leave the blocks free to expand sideways; the non-matching interface must not hold them

quantities.quantity: Finite: the contact pressure at the secondary node (0.5, 0.5, 1) over −σ_zz of element 19
quantities.reason: the mortar multipliers are the nodal values of the contact pressure, uniform and equal to the stress across the interface

quantities.quantity: Finite: the integrated contact pressure over the reaction at the pushed top
quantities.reason: the pressure carries the whole load across the interface

quantities.quantity: Small: σ_zz of element 19 (uniaxial stress E ε = −10 for the 1% squeeze)
quantities.reason: the squeeze less the penetration the augmented Lagrangian leaves (up to 10⁻⁵ of the element thickness, a few 10⁻⁵ of the squeeze)
